title: Q-RES-perez-lopez-1974-P6: A memory that leaves past mistakes out (measured 0.692, target >= 1.0)
body:
**Owner:** product-manager
**Trigger:** research pass: perez-lopez-1974 finding P6 is not-met (measured 0.692)
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation research --probe perez-lopez-1974:P6
**Prediction:** lessons_enforced_share >= 1 within 336 h
**Out of scope:** editing the study, its target or the paper to match the code; the measurement is changed only by changing the mechanism
**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation research --probe perez-lopez-1974:P6`
**Status:** closed

Concern: A memory that leaves past mistakes out. The study: Selective use of memory is central: an evoked set can leave out what shows that previous actions were wrong. The working paper defines "pride" as the attitude "which tends to eliminate from the 'evoked set' all those elements in memory which show that previous actions were wrong". A system that records its mistakes but lets nothing act on them has that blind spot.

Mechanisms that should answer it: LESSONS-1 (foundation/lessons.py); FAILURE-RESOLVE-1 (foundation/failure_audit.py).

Metric: share of recorded lessons bound to a check, variable, detector or test (doctrine/lessons.json), target >= 1.0. Improve the mechanism (or add one) until the probe passes; the white paper at /research updates itself from the same measurement.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-27T17:07:39Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.0 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
